adoption.notes: The runtime verifies each firmware fault under its own v: v 1 under v1's closed sets, v 2 under this version's, any other v refused, and drives this version's corpus through its ingest gate. Its module docstring and capability matrix describe the v 2 sets as this draft's and make no conformance claim, so the version is not frozen by this merge. It verifies signatures with OpenSSL behind its ed25519-key-admission/v1 admission. That combination reaches every verdict of the ed25519-verification/v1 corpus when the corpus is run on the host, OpenSSL alone differing only on the keys admission refuses, but the runtime does not yet drive that corpus through its ingest gate.

The device signs every fault at v 2 and has no path to v 1; faults it buffered before adopting are retransmitted at v 1 as stored. It mirrors this version's corpus byte for byte. Its DECISIONS.md says core/fault_event.c implements the fault object this version defines; that sentence was written while the firmware was built alongside this draft, and the maintainer ruled on 2026-10-09 that it is provenance, not a conformance claim, so the version is not frozen by this merge and stays amendable.

notes: Exists so a device can sign a command_rejected fault whose detail is rate_limited: the fault object carries v 2, under which the closed detail sets are the ones this version lists. Manifest, envelope and maintenance events keep v 1. The runtime verifies v 2 faults and the edge firmware signs them; the evidence authority and sdk-python have not adopted it. Every verifier, the runtime first, adopts it before the devices whose faults it reads: a v1-only verifier refuses every v 2 fault.
